$comment: Allowlist of permitted RUNTIME dependencies. Enforced by scripts/check-dependencies.mjs
in CI. devDependencies are not restricted - they do not ship.
Adding an entry here is the review gate. The question is not 'does this package work'
but 'is the platform genuinely insufficient'. See docs/adr/0013-minimal-runtime-dependencies.md.
Before adding anything, check the platform: fetch, node:crypto (incl. JWT sign/verify and
JWK import), crypto.randomUUID, structuredClone, Intl. The whole auth and CouchDB path
was verified to need no dependencies at all.

allowed.@lit/localize: Runtime locale switching plus message extraction tooling.
allowed.pouchdb-browser: The CouchDB replication protocol: revision trees, conflict detection, resumable sync. ADR 0002 rejected writing this by hand because it is the hard part.
allowed.pdf-lib: PDF writing with font embedding (ADR 0007). Not reasonable to hand-roll.
allowed.@zxing/browser: QR decoding where BarcodeDetector is missing, which is every iOS Safari. Must be lazily loaded so native-API browsers never download it.
allowed.fastify: HTTP server for the API (ADR 0004). Predates this policy; ADR 0013 notes node:http as the alternative if the API stays thin.
allowed.@noble/hashes: Identical hashing in Node and the browser. node:crypto and WebCrypto diverge in the fine print, and code shared between packages/api and packages/web must not depend on which runtime it lands in. Audited, zero dependencies.
allowed.@noble/curves: As @noble/hashes, for elliptic curve operations. Depends only on @noble/hashes.
allowed.@noble/ciphers: As @noble/hashes, for symmetric encryption. Zero dependencies.
allowed.@matter-manager/core: The workspace domain package. Pure, no dependencies of its own.

banned.nano: Predates native fetch and carries its own HTTP stack. Use fetch.
banned.jose: node:crypto signs and verifies ES256/RS256 and imports JWKs directly. Verified.
banned.jwk-to-pem: createPublicKey({ key, format: 'jwk' }) does this natively.
banned.date-fns: Use Intl unless a specific gap is demonstrated.
banned.workbox-window: The service worker is hand-written; see ADR 0013.

allowedDev.$comment: Build-only tooling permitted as a devDependency in a package that ships a bundle. Anything here must be provably absent from the built output.
allowedDev.@vitest/browser: Runs packages/web's tests in a real browser instead of jsdom. Test-only, never imported by src.
allowedDev.playwright: Browser automation driving @vitest/browser's Chromium instance. Test-only, never imported by src.
allowedDev.@open-wc/testing-helpers: DOM/component test utilities (fixture, waitUntil) for web component tests. Test-only, never imported by src.
allowedDev.@types/node: Type declarations only (import.meta.dirname, node:fs in tests). Erased at compile time, never imported by src.
allowedDev.vite: The dev/build/preview bundler and vitest's browser-mode dependency. Provably absent from the built output: it produces dist/, it is not part of it - the bundled bundle never imports its own bundler.
allowedDev.pouchdb-core: PouchDB without any adapter, used only by packages/data's tests. The shipping build is pouchdb-browser, which packages/web supplies; pouchdb-browser references `self` at module scope and cannot be imported in Node at all, which is why the tests use core plus the memory adapter. Proven absent from src by packages/data/test/no-pouchdb-import.test.ts.
allowedDev.pouchdb-adapter-memory: The in-memory storage adapter the data tests run against, so no test ever touches a real CouchDB. Same proof as pouchdb-core.
allowedDev.@types/pouchdb-core: Type declarations for PouchDB.Database, the only PouchDB name packages/data/src mentions. Erased at compile time.
allowedDev.@types/pouchdb-adapter-memory: Type declarations that add the memory adapter to PouchDB.Configuration. Test-only, erased at compile time.
